newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Colgate-Palmolive gets partial OK of Brazil buyout.
newsitem.headline: Colgate-Palmolive gets partial OK of Brazil buyout.

text.p: Brazil has approved Colgate-Palmolive's $1.04 billion acquisition of the Brazilian oral hygiene firm Anakol, but the U.S. consumer products giant must opt for one of three tough conditions linked to the approval.
The government's anti-trust body -- the Administrative Economic Defence Council -- voted late Wednesday in favour of the acquisition.

But it gave the company three options, either it must agree not to sell the Kolynos brand of toothpaste produced by Anakol for four years or license Kolynos to a third party over a 20-year period or sell the Kolynos brand to a competitor with a less than one percent share of the market.
Colgate-Palmolive has 60 days to choose one of the options.
Kolynos accounts for 50 percent of Brazilian toothpaste sales and gave Colgate-Palmolive a roughly 77 percent total share of the market.
Anakol makes Kolynos in several Latin American countries. The Brazilian operations accounted for $760 million of the 1995 buyout.
The anti-trust agency investigated the deal to see if it stifled competition in Brazil or prevented new players from entering the market.
It did not impose any restrictions on Kolynos' other oral hygiene products, like toothbrushes and mouthwashes.
